newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts to recapture 114-24 high on way up.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts to recapture 114-24 high on way up.

text.p: June gilt futures will aim to retake the contract high at 114-24 on the way up to more lofty territory, bolstered by a solid close in the previous session, technical analysts said on Tuesday.

"Yesterday we came back and tested support at 113-29 and bounced straight back up and had a nice positive close which suggests we're going to try and stretch a bit higher," Elizabeth Miller, technical analyst at Deustche Morgan Grenfell in London, said.
The first target this session will be the contract high at 114-24, hit on Monday.
Gilts were quoted at 114-08, down 6/32 just after the open at 0700 GMT.
Miller said beyond the contract high, gilts would challenge the 115-00 psychological level.
She said the big level on the upside however, was 115-26, a 76.4 Fibonacci retracement of the drop from a high of 121-06 in December 1993 to 98-14 in September 1994 on monthly continuation charts.
"On the downside we have support at yesterday's low of 113-29," Miller said. The contract also hit a low of 113-30 on Friday.
"If we break through there then we'll head down towards 112-28 which was the low from May 8," Miller said.
Technical analysts at Royal Bank of Scotland in London also expected the contract to track higher after Monday's price action, despite overbought conditions beginning to emerge.

"For the moment this condition is being ignored and this will the case again today if the June hurdles resistance at 114-18," they said in a research note. But they expected that to form a barrier for now.
Daily charts show the contract hitting a high on Monday of 114-16.
September short sterling was quoted at 93.27, unchanged at 0732 GMT.
"If we can get through there there's no reason why we can't stretch to 93.38," she said. Beyond there the high at 93.48 beckoned.
On the downside support arrives at Monday's low of 93.24, which was also Friday's high. Below there 93.20 and 93.16 would act as buffers.
